findings.title: limitFunction no longer forwards call arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper was changed to `return () => limit(() => function_());`, dropping the rest parameters that should be forwarded to `function_`.
findings.impact: Any consumer using `limitFunction` with arguments gets incorrect runtime behavior. The TypeScript declaration still returns `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`, so typed callers can pass values that are silently discarded.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-125 drops arguments. index.d.ts:133-136 declares the returned function with the original argument list. `git show HEAD:index.js` shows the previous implementation returned `(...arguments_) => limit(() => function_(...arguments_))`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory Node probe of current index.js with only `yocto-queue` shimmed: `const limited = limitFunction((...args) => args, {concurrency: 1}); await limited('a', 'b')` returned `[]`.

findings.title: Options-object default now rejects clearQueue pending tasks
findings.cause: Object option destructuring changed the default from `rejectOnClear = false` to `rejectOnClear = true`.
findings.impact: `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` now rejects queued promises with `AbortError` when `clearQueue()` is called, even though the public README and type comments document the default as false. This is a breaking behavior change for callers that clear queues during shutdown and expect pending promises to remain unresolved/discarded.
findings.evidence: index.js:6 destructures `rejectOnClear = true`. readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 state `rejectOnClear` is a boolean with default false. `git show HEAD:index.js` shows the previous default was false.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory Node probe: create `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, enqueue one running task and one pending task, call `limit.clearQueue()`. The pending task settled as `{state: 'rejected', name: 'AbortError'}`.

findings.title: rejectOnClear validation accepts falsey non-booleans
findings.cause: The validation guard was weakened from `typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean'` to `rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean'`, so only truthy invalid values are rejected.
findings.impact: Invalid configuration such as `rejectOnClear: 0` or `rejectOnClear: ''` is silently accepted, contradicting the documented boolean-only option and making clearQueue behavior depend on JavaScript truthiness instead of the API contract.
findings.evidence: index.js:11-13 only validates when `rejectOnClear` is truthy. readme.md:46-49 documents the option as boolean. index.test-d.ts:29 includes a type-level expectation that non-boolean `rejectOnClear` is invalid.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory Node probe: `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})` and `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: ''})` both returned successfully instead of throwing `TypeError`.

findings.title: limit.map omits index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The mapper call now passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`, so sets, generators, and array iterators do not receive their positional index.
findings.impact: The README and TypeScript API promise an index for every iterable. Callers mapping a `Set`, generator, or iterator and using the index receive `undefined`, causing wrong results such as `NaN`, duplicate keys, or lost ordering metadata.
findings.evidence: index.js:106-115 gates the index on `Array.isArray(iterable)`. readme.md:78-84 says the mapper receives the item value and index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`. index.d.ts:40-43 types the second mapper argument as `number` for `Iterable<Input>`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory Node probe: `limit.map(['a','b'], (_v, index) => index)` returned `[0,1]`, but `limit.map(new Set(['a','b']), (_v, index) => index)` and `limit.map(['a','b'].values(), (_v, index) => index)` returned `[undefined, undefined]` (serialized as `[null,null]`).

findings.title: Infinity concurrency support was removed
findings.cause: The validator no longer permits `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`; it now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency)`.
findings.impact: Existing callers using `pLimit(Infinity)` as a no-limit mode now get a `TypeError`, even though the prior implementation explicitly accepted positive infinity and the error text still describes `number from 1 and up`.
findings.evidence: index.js:127-131 rejects non-integers. `git diff -- index.js` shows the removed `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` branch, and `git show HEAD:index.js` shows the previous validator allowed it.
findings.reproduction_or_test: In-memory Node probe: `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` threw `TypeError: Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`.
